page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic instructions. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25% at 2678.09. Most other metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1489.0) and multi-core (5922.0) scores, fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is stable, measuring 509.47 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 57.86 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 34.57 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds for a medium 7B model are also limited, with prompt processing dropping to a weak 16.86 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-8 offers a high-density memory configuration relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration means it is not designed for high-speed local disk I/O or heavy graphics and deep learning training tasks, but rather for structured data processing and general-purpose memory-heavy workloads.
